basis: Skin, thyroid and airway ciliary defects define syndrome; lacrimal dysfunction 30-79%. Enteropathy is described but its frequency is unclear and the four-axis cap favors ocular evidence.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: enteropathy is described without frequency; the four-axis cap favors ocular dysfunction with explicit 30-79% frequency.
decisions.ocular: involved: lacrimal dysfunction affects 30-79%, supporting loss of lacrimal function; ophthalmic complications also appear in the definition.

basis: Deglycosylation disorder with defining brain malformations and developmental disability; tongue hamartoma 2/6 (33%). Microtia 2/5 lacks established impairment; hearing loss 1/4 is below threshold.

decisions.neurologic: primary: brain malformations and developmental disability characterize the syndrome; motor and speech delay 4/4, cerebellar hypoplasia 4/5, intellectual disability 3/4.
decisions.otologic: none: microtia in 2/5 establishes ear morphology, not functional damage; documented hearing impairment is 1/4 (25%).

basis: Epiphyseal dysplasia, vitreoretinal degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss form the defining COL9A1 Stickler phenotype; hearing impairment is documented in 6/6.

decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural hearing impairment is a defining component of COL9A1 Stickler syndrome, documented in 6/6 assessed patients.

basis: Developmental disability and cataracts define syndrome; renal dysplasia 1/3 and cleft palate 1/3 (33%) support involvement. Unspecified heart morphology and minor skeletal features lack clear damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is a structural oral defect in 1/3 assessed patients (~33%); it is part of the syndrome rather than a separate acquired disease.

basis: Defining elliptocytosis, hearing loss and nephrocalcinosis; cleft palate 2/2. Clubfoot (1/2) and PDA (1/1) omitted at cap; facial hypoplasia alone does not establish locomotor damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft hard palate/submucous cleft palate in 2/2 assessed patients is a direct structural oral defect, prioritized under the four-axis cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none under cap: clubfoot is reported in 1/2; palatal defects in 2/2 receive the fourth axis. Midface hypoplasia alone is dysmorphism without established locomotor impairment.

basis: [MedGen](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/medgen/338528) documents metabolic abnormality, growth delay and intellectual disability; the erythrocyte T-antigen interpretation is unsupported.

decisions.haematologic: none: OMIM 276200 refers to a poorly characterized metabolic/neurodevelopmental phenotype; evidence does not support an erythrocyte T-antigen disorder.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is a documented characteristic of this poorly characterized syndrome.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: documented metabolic/homeostatic abnormality and the historical urinary T-substance phenotype support a metabolic disorder.

basis: Mature B-cell leukemia involving marrow, blood and spleen; its indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma classification also invokes the lymphoma mechanism axis.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: classified among non-Hodgkin lymphomas in [SEER](https://seer.cancer.gov/csr/1975_2017/results_merged/sect_19_nhl.pdf); the supplied ancestry also identifies indolent B-cell NHL.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency intrinsically impairs T- and B-lymphocyte function, satisfying immune and blood-cell axes; infections are separate diseases and other organ damage varies across subtypes.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the definition specifies intrinsic dysfunction of blood lymphocytes. The blood-cell disease rule does not require reduced cell counts.

basis: Hereditary motor neuronopathy; established upper- and lower-limb muscle atrophy in 1/2 (50%) represents tissue loss within the disease, beyond weakness alone.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: established muscle atrophy in 1/2 (50%) represents structural muscle loss from disease-related denervation; it is not merely weakness or a separately coded comorbidity.

basis: Motor-neuron disease, epilepsy and progressive muscle atrophy define this sphingolipidosis; atrophy 6/6. Respiratory muscle weakness does not establish lung damage; aspiration pneumonia is separate.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: progressive muscular atrophy is explicitly part of the disease definition and documented in 6/6; denervation explains the muscle tissue loss without removing this defining organ.
